item.title: Remember: trim trees September through December
item.description: Spring is here, and nesting season is in full swing for our local birds. One way we can help protect them is by scheduling tree and shrub trimming during months that end in “BER,” September through December. item.title: Remembering a local arts titan
item.description: Margaret Travers, a beloved member of our arts community, passed away recently. She left a legacy that is unequalled, and Thousand Oaks and Ventura County are better for it. When it came to the arts, whether visual, literary or performing, Margaret not only supported it, but encouraged it to blossom. Many artists thrived here because of her encouragement. item.title: NIMBYs don’t consider the facts
item.description: I shake my head as I read the recent housing articles and accompanying letters, reminding myself of that famous line about insanity. item.description: I am increasingly confused by the contradictions in how CVUSD approaches technology, particularly when it comes to YouTube. item.title: Federal dollars flow freely, but the bill is coming due
item.description: A March 13 visit by Congressmember Julia Brownley to the Conejo Valley was, by any local measure, a success. Nearly $2.8 million in federal funding will support projects that promise tangible public benefits: cleaner stormwater systems, enhanced streetscapes, improved energy resilience and more reliable water infrastructure through the Calleguas Municipal Water District. item.title: Big blazes spur big legislative action
item.description: Spurred by devastating wildfires in Los Angeles and across the Central Coast, a bipartisan group of state lawmakers has introduced a sweeping legislative package aimed at reshaping how California prepares for megafires. The “2026 Joint Megafire Prevention Package” includes more than a dozen bills addressing home hardening, resilience financing and the expansion of “beneficial fire” practices. item.description: Thousand Oaks’ 30-year-old museum celebrating the area’s first inhabitants is once again facing hard economic times.
